newsitem.title: USA: U.S. August existing home sales fell 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. August existing home sales fell 0.5 pct.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes fell 0.5 percent in August to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.13 million units from a revised 4.15 million units in July, the National Association of Realtors said Wednesday.
The August sales rate was up 2.0 percent from sales of 4.05 million in August last year.
Previously, NAR said July sales of existing homes fell 0.5 percent to a seasonally adjusted 4.14 million units.
Wall Street economists had forecast August sales of 4.09 million units.

NAR Chief Economist John Tuccillo said the slight drop in sales last month was to be expected.

"The nation's housing market has seen unprecedented movements this year, and it's only natural that the market will correct itself," he said. "The nation's housing market is easing in for a soft landing."
NAR officials said the recent sales pace remained impressive, and cited a stable economy and falling interest rates which are back to levels seen in the early spring.
